At the request of an Indian Tribe, Tribal organization authorized by an Indian Tribe, or inter-Tribal consortium selected under this section, if the Secretary determines the request to be reasonable, the Secretary shall waive any matching requirement that would otherwise apply to the Indian Tribe, Tribal organization, or inter-Tribal consortium under an included program covered by a compact or funding agreement under this section.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall implement each provision of this section, and each provision of a compact or funding agreement entered into or modified pursuant to this section, in a manner consistent with title V of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act, except the Secretary may make reasonable modifications—

paragraph.text: to comply with the provisions of this title when the provisions of this title conflict with the provisions of title V of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act; and

to the extent necessary to fulfill the policies described in the declaration of policy in section 3 of title V of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act relating to Tribal administration of programs, services, functions, or activities (or portions thereof) pursuant to title V of such Act.

At the request of an Indian Tribe, Tribal organization authorized by an Indian Tribe, or inter-Tribal consortium, if the Secretary determines that a waiver would further the declaration of policy under section 3 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act, the Secretary shall grant a waiver of statutory, regulatory, or program requirements to facilitate the ability of an Indian Tribe, Tribal organization authorized by an Indian Tribe, or inter-Tribal consortium to redesign or consolidate included programs or reallocate funds.
The Secretary shall document all requests for a waiver under paragraph (1), including a description of—

subparagraph.text: the reasons for each request;
the effect of the waiver on the Indian Tribe, authorized Tribal organization, or inter-Tribal consortium making the request; and
the views of the Indian Tribe, authorized Tribal organization, or inter-Tribal consortium regarding the requested waiver.

paragraph.text: Waiver requests shall be subject to the final offer process described in section 507(b) of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act.

subsection.text: Unless expressly agreed to by an Indian Tribe, Tribal organization authorized by an Indian Tribe, or inter-Tribal consortium in a compact of funding agreement entered into or modified pursuant to this section, an Indian Tribe, Tribal organization, or inter-Tribal consortium selected under this section shall not be subject to any agency circular, policy, manual, guidance, or regulation.
The following provisions of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act shall apply to a compact or funding agreement under this title:

paragraph.text: Section 102(d).
Subsections (b), (c)(1), (c)(2), (d), (e), and (h) of section 506.
Subsections (g), (h), and (i) of section 508.

The Director of the Office of Tribal Self-Governance of the Department of Health and Human Services shall provide technical assistance to the Secretary and participating Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations to carry out this section, including technical assistance to Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations to conduct evaluations of programs for which such Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations have participated in self-governance under this section.

The Secretary shall award grants to national organizations with expertise on Tribal self-governance, for purposes of providing technical assistance to Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations in the negotiation of self-governance compact or funding agreements described in subsection (a).

subparagraph.text: There are authorized to be appropriated—

clause.text: $2,000,000 to carry out the technical assistance grants under paragraph (2); and
such sums as necessary to provide technical assistance under paragraph (1).

subparagraph.text: Amounts made available pursuant to subparagraph (A) shall remain available until expended.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall conduct Tribal consultation before promulgating regulations to carry out this section.
The Secretary, in consultation with the participating Indian Tribes and inter-Tribal consortia, shall submit to Congress annual reports on the implementation of this section.
In this section:

paragraph.text: The term covered program means any mental health, substance abuse prevention and treatment, recovery support, crisis response, suicide prevention, or related behavioral health program of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration as the Secretary determines appropriate.

The term funding agreement means a negotiated agreement between the Secretary and an Indian Tribe or inter-Tribal consortium that specifies the programs, services, functions, and activities to be performed by such Indian Tribe or Tribal organization.
The terms Indian Tribe and Tribal organization have the meanings given such terms in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act.
The term inter-Tribal consortium has the meaning given the term in section 501 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act.

The term self-governance compact means a negotiated agreement between the Secretary and an Indian Tribe, inter-Tribal consortium, or a Tribal organization authorized by an Indian Tribe that establishes the general terms of the relationship between the Secretary and such Indian Tribe or inter-Tribal consortium.

section.header: Native Children's Environmental Health Protection Task Force
section.text: The Indian Health Care Improvement Act is amended by inserting after section 223 (25 U.S.C. 1621v) the following:

section.header: Native Children's Environmental Health Protection Task Force

paragraph.text: There is established within the Council on Environmental Quality a Native Children's Environmental Health Protection Task Force (referred to in this section as the Task Force).
The Task Force—

subparagraph.text: shall include—

clause.text: the Chair of the Council on Environmental Quality, who shall serve as Chairperson of the Task Force; and
1 representative from each of—

subclause.text: the Department of Health and Human Services, including the Service;
the Environmental Protection Agency;
the Department of Housing and Urban Development;
the Department of the Interior;
the Department of Agriculture;
the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention;
the Department of Transportation;
tribal organizations;
Tribal environmental health programs;
Tribal health directors; and
the organization described in section 12(7) of the Native Hawaiian Health Care Improvement Act (42 U.S.C. 11711(7)); and

subparagraph.text: may include a representative of Native youth.

subsection.text: The purpose of the Task Force shall be to serve as a coordinating body to protect the environmental health of Native children through cross-agency collaboration, including by—

paragraph.text: identifying and addressing environmental health hazards that disproportionately affect Native children;
enhancing coordination among Federal, State, and Tribal agencies, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations on environmental health issues affecting Native children;
developing and implementing culturally appropriate solutions to environmental health challenges in Native communities;
leveraging resources across Federal, State, and Tribal agencies to maximize impact and efficiency of environmental health programs that serve Native communities;
strengthening capacity among Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations to address environmental health threats through technical assistance and resource sharing;
ensuring environmental health interventions respect Tribal sovereignty and incorporate traditional ecological knowledge;
promoting environmental justice for Native children and their communities; and
reducing administrative burdens on Tribal-serving and Native Hawaiian-serving environmental health programs through streamlined processes and integrated systems.

subsection.text: The Task Force shall develop and implement a comprehensive strategic plan to address environmental health threats to Native children, including dust, mold, sanitation challenges, contaminated lands from mining, industrial wastes, abandoned uranium mines, pesticides from agricultural operations, oil spills, groundwater contamination, wildfire smoke inhalation, and other natural disasters.

The Task Force shall consult and engage with Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations, as appropriate, in developing and implementing all protocols and processes under this section.
Annually, the Task Force shall submit to Congress a report on the implementation of this section, including any outcomes and recommendations, as applicable.

section.header: Integration of environmental health within primary care

subsection.text: Section 107 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act (25 U.S.C. 1616) is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall ensure that all health professional training programs administered by the Service include mandatory training on—

subparagraph.text: environmental health assessment protocols specific to Tribal communities;
recognition of environmental health issues affecting Native children;
home environmental assessment procedures and documentation;
cultural competency in discussing environmental health concerns with Tribal families; and
integration of traditional ecological knowledge in environmental health assessments.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall develop the training components described in paragraph (1) in consultation with—

subparagraph.text: the Division of Environmental Health Services of the Service;
Tribal environmental health programs;
Tribal Epidemiology Centers;
Tribal health boards; and
pediatric environmental health specialty units.

subsection.text: Title II of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act (25 U.S.C. 1621 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Comprehensive health system

subsection.text: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this section, the Service shall establish a comprehensive environmental health system (referred to in this section as the system) that includes—

paragraph.text: electronic health record capabilities for—

subparagraph.text: standardized environmental exposure history documentation;
automated clinical decision support for environmental health concerns;
bi-directional data sharing between clinical and environmental health services; and
geographic tracking of environmental health conditions; and

paragraph.text: standardized referral protocols that—

subparagraph.text: connect clinical providers with environmental health services;
establish response time requirements;
require documented follow-up; and
include case management when needed.

subsection.text: In implementing the system, the Secretary shall offer to enter into memoranda of agreement with Service units, Tribal environmental programs, and relevant Federal and State agencies.
Annually, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on system implementation, utilization, and outcomes.
There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2032.

title.header: Improving nutrition programs for Native children, youth, and families

section.header: Tribal pilot programs for SNAP administration
section.text: The Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 (7 U.S.C. 2011 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Tribal pilot programs for SNAP administration

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term Tribal pilot participant means a covered Indian entity (as defined in subsection (b)(1)) or an Indian Tribe that is participating in a pilot program under this section.
The term Tribal service population means households residing within the service area identified by, as applicable—

subparagraph.text: a covered Indian entity (as defined in subsection (b)(1)) under subsection (b)(4)(A)(iii); or
an Indian Tribe under subsection (c)(2)(A)(iii).

paragraph.text: In this subsection, the term covered Indian entity means—

subparagraph.text: each of the 12 regional nonprofit corporations established pursuant to the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.); and
the Metlakatla Indian Community of the Annette Islands Reserve.

paragraph.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall establish a pilot program (referred to in this subsection as the pilot program) under which the Secretary shall award a grant to at least 1 covered Indian entity each fiscal year to administer all or portions of the supplemental nutrition assistance program within the Tribal service area of the covered Indian entity.
The term of a grant awarded under the pilot program shall be 3 years, which may be extended for an additional 3 years, as determined by the Secretary.

subparagraph.text: A covered Indian entity seeking a grant under the pilot program shall submit to the Secretary a 3-year plan that—

clause.text: describes how the covered Indian entity will administer the supplemental nutrition assistance program consistent with this Act;
specifies whether benefits and administrative functions will be provided directly or through agreements, contracts, compacts, or consortia arrangements;
identifies the Tribal service populations and service areas to be served;

identifies employment opportunities in or near the service areas and the manner in which the covered Indian entity will cooperate in enhancing those opportunities consistent with applicable Federal standards; and
describes financial management, program integrity, accountability, and data security procedures.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall review the plan submitted under subparagraph (A) in accordance with subsection (e).
Not later than 90 days after receiving a plan under subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall approve or deny the plan.

The amount of a grant awarded to a covered Indian entity under the pilot program shall be the amount attributable to expenditures for Tribal service populations identified under paragraph (3)(A)(iii).

clause.text: The Secretary shall use data submitted by the State of Alaska to calculate the payment amount under subparagraph (A).
If a covered Indian entity disagrees with the data described in clause (i), the covered Indian entity may submit additional information to the Secretary for consideration.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall reduce the Federal administrative payments otherwise payable to the State of Alaska under section 16 by the amount attributable to administrative functions assumed by a covered Indian entity receiving a grant under the pilot program.

Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall establish a pilot program (referred to in this subsection as the pilot program) under which the Secretary shall award grants to at least 5 Indian Tribes to administer all or portions of the supplemental nutrition assistance program within Tribal service areas.

subparagraph.text: An Indian Tribe seeking a grant under the pilot program shall submit to the Secretary a plan that—

clause.text: describes how the Indian Tribe will administer the supplemental nutrition assistance program consistent with this Act;
specifies whether benefits and administrative functions will be provided directly or through agreements, contracts, or compacts, including agreements with relevant State agencies;
identifies the Tribal service populations and service areas to be served;
describes financial management, program integrity, accountability, and data security procedures; and
identifies employment opportunities in or near the service areas and the manner in which the Indian Tribe will cooperate in enhancing those opportunities consistent with applicable Federal standards.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall review the plan submitted under subparagraph (A) in accordance with subsection (e).
Not later than 90 days after receiving a plan under subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall approve or deny the plan.

paragraph.text: Each Indian Tribe participating in the pilot program shall enter into a cooperative agreement with the Secretary and the applicable State agency regarding administration, data sharing, eligibility coordination, program integrity, and operational responsibilities.

subparagraph.text: For the first fiscal year in which the pilot program is implemented, the Secretary shall select at least 5 Indian Tribes to participate in the pilot program.
For each fiscal year following the first fiscal year described in subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall approve participation in the pilot program of not more than 5 additional Indian Tribes.

In selecting Indian Tribes to participate in the pilot program, the Secretary shall prioritize geographic diversity, demonstrated administrative capacity, and Tribal communities that have previously worked with States on administering the supplemental nutrition assistance program in those communities.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall provide funding directly to Indian Tribes participating in the pilot program without requiring pass-through agreements with States.

subsection.text: In participating in a pilot program under this section, a Tribal pilot participant shall—

paragraph.text: subject to waiver by the Secretary, comply with requirements comparable to requirements applicable to State agencies administering the supplemental nutrition assistance program;
prohibit households from receiving duplicative assistance;
comply with section 5(f)(1) of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5305(f)(1)); and
maintain fiscal accountability consistent with generally accepted accounting principles.

In reviewing a plan under subsection (b)(3) or (c)(2), the Secretary shall consider the demonstrated administrative capacity of the Tribal pilot participant, which may include experience administering federally funded Tribal programs, including—

subparagraph.text: a Tribal family assistance program operated under section 412 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 612);
programs operated under contracts or compacts authorized by the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.);
employment and training programs under section 6(d)(4);
programs administered under the Indian Employment, Training and Related Services Demonstration Act of 1992 (25 U.S.C. 3401 et seq.); or
other public assistance, nutrition, workforce development, or social service programs administered by the Tribal pilot participant.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall not impose on Tribal pilot participants requirements relating to administrative capacity that are more burdensome than requirements applied to States administering the supplemental nutrition assistance program.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall provide funding to a Tribal organization to provide technical assistance, training, and implementation support to Tribal pilot participants to facilitate successful administration of the pilot programs under this section.

paragraph.text: Households within a Tribal service population that is served pursuant to this section shall not be included in calculating under this Act—

subparagraph.text: any State payment error rate;
any State matching fund requirement;
any State financial liability or penalty relating to payment accuracy; or
any State cost obligation under section 4(a)(2).

paragraph.text: Of the administrative costs incurred by Tribal pilot participants under this section—

subparagraph.text: 100 percent shall be reimbursed by the Secretary; and
0 percent shall be subject to administrative cost-sharing requirements applicable to States under section 16.

paragraph.text: Nothing in this section affects the application of subparagraphs (F) and (G) of section 6(o)(3).
A State shall not be penalized, financially or administratively, based on Tribal service populations that are served pursuant to this section, including with respect to—

subparagraph.text: matching fund requirements;
administrative cost-sharing requirements;
work requirement compliance calculations;
payment error rates; or
administrative performance measures.

subsection.text: Not later than 5 years after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall evaluate, and submit to Congress a report on, with respect to the pilot programs carried out under this section—

paragraph.text: participant access and food security outcomes;
administrative efficiency;
payment accuracy and program integrity;
Tribal self-sufficiency outcomes; and
recommendations relating to whether those pilot programs should be continued, expanded, modified, or made permanent.

subsection.text: Nothing in this section diminishes—

paragraph.text: the trust responsibility of the United States to Indian Tribes; or
the sovereign authority of Indian Tribes.

section.header: Child nutrition programs Tribal pilot projects

paragraph.text: The Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, in partnership with the Secretary of Agriculture, shall conduct a study on the intersection of nutrition programs and health outcomes for Native children in American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian communities.
The study under paragraph (1) shall examine—

subparagraph.text: health outcomes from Federal nutrition programs in American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian communities;
integration of traditional foods in Federal nutrition assistance;
community-level nutrition intervention effectiveness;
food sovereignty and community health connections; and
coordinated nutrition-health service delivery models.

section.header: Program for housing assistance for homeless American Indians and Alaska Natives

subsection.text: Title VII of the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 (25 U.S.C. 4211 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Program for housing assistance for homeless American Indians and Alaska Natives

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term American Indians and Alaska Natives means individuals who are regarded as American Indian or Alaska Native by the Indian or Alaska Native community in which the individual lives, as evidenced by tribal membership, enrollment, eligibility for enrollment, active participation in tribal affairs, or other indicia of community affiliation.
The term domestic violence has the meaning given the term in section 40002(a) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (34 U.S.C. 12291(a)).

paragraph.header: Eligible American Indians and Alaska Natives
paragraph.text: The term eligible American Indians and Alaska Natives means American Indians and Alaska Natives who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, as defined by the Indian tribe.

The term eligible recipient means an Indian tribe, or a tribally designated housing entity or tribal organization designated by such Indian tribe to apply for a grant on its behalf under this section.
The term homeless youth has the meaning given the term in section 387 of the Runaway and Homeless Youth Act (34 U.S.C. 11279).
The term Program means the program established under subsection (b).

paragraph.header: Secretary of Health and Human Services
paragraph.text: The term Secretary of Health and Human Services means the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Indian Health Service.

The Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall establish and administer a grant program to provide rental assistance and supportive housing services to be known as the Tribal Homeless Housing Assistance Grant Program for American Indians and Alaska Natives who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
The purpose of this section is to establish a supportive housing competitive grant program that—

subparagraph.text: provides rental assistance for American Indians and Alaska Natives who are homeless or at risk of homelessness;
integrates supportive services and case management;
prioritizes homeless youth, families with children, and survivors of domestic violence;
strengthens tribal self-determination in housing administration; and
reduces and prevents homelessness in tribal communities and Native populations.

paragraph.text: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the Secretary shall administer the Program in a manner similar to the program under section 8(o)(19) of the United States Housing Act of 1937 (42 U.S.C. 1437f(o)(19)) and the demonstration program established under paragraph (5) under the heading Tenant-based rental assistance under the heading Public and Indian Housing in title II of division K of the Consolidated and Further Continuing Appropriations Act, 2015 (Public Law 113–235; 128 Stat. 2732), in accordance with the regulations promulgated to carry out those programs.

Of the amounts made available for grants under title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11360 et seq.) each fiscal year, the Secretary may make available not more than 5 percent to carry out this section.

subsection.text: The Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall consult with eligible recipients to ensure effective delivery of grants under the Program.

Each eligible recipient applying for a grant under the Program shall submit to the Secretary an application that describes how the eligible recipient will provide 2 years of mandatory case management services to eligible American Indians and Alaska Natives under the Program, including in partnership with other qualified organizations or the Indian Health Service, when appropriate.

subparagraph.text: An eligible recipient receiving a grant under the Program—

clause.text: may use the grant to provide supportive services to eligible American Indians and Alaska Natives; and

shall determine the supportive services that are necessary and appropriate to prevent or end homelessness, reducing housing instability, preserving family unity where housing instability is a contributing factor, or promote long-term housing stability.

subparagraph.text: An eligible recipient receiving a grant under the Program shall determine the nature, scope, and delivery of supportive services described in subparagraph (A), which may include services to address behavioral health needs, substance use disorders, transportation barriers, employment and education needs, child welfare involvement, domestic violence, or other barriers to housing stability identified by the eligible recipient.
The Secretary—

clause.text: shall defer to the determination of an eligible recipient regarding the design, scope, and delivery of supportive services under subparagraph (B), including culturally appropriate and traditional services identified by the eligible recipient; and

may not require a showing that a specific service category is authorized under any other Federal housing or homeless assistance program, provided that the eligible recipient determines and documents that the services are reasonably related to the housing stability for eligible American Indians and Alaska Natives.

paragraph.text: An eligible recipient that receives a grant under the Program shall prioritize providing assistance to homeless youth, families with children, and survivors of domestic violence.

subsection.text: Grants awarded under the Program shall be based on need, administrative capacity, service of homeless youth, families with children and survivors of domestic violence, and other criteria established by the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services and eligible recipients.

The Secretary may waive, or specify alternative requirements for, any provision of any statute or regulation that the Secretary administers in connection with the use of funds made available under the Program (except for requirements related to fair housing, nondiscrimination, and labor standards), upon a finding by the Secretary that any such waiver or alternative requirement is necessary for the effective delivery and administration of such assistance.
The Secretary may set aside amounts made available under subsection (b)(4) for renewal grants under the Program and define renewal criteria, including data reporting.

Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of the Native Children’s Commission Implementation Act of 2026, and every 5 years thereafter, the Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall review and submit to Congress a report on the implementation of the Program, including any recommendations to improve the Program and its implementation.

section.header: Tribal Continuum of Care Participation Grant Program

subsection.text: Title VII of the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 (25 U.S.C. 4211 et seq.), as amended by section 601 of this title, is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Tribal Continuum of Care Participation Grant Program

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term eligible entity means an Indian tribe and a tribally designated housing entity.
The term Program means the program established under subsection (b).

The Secretary shall establish and administer a grant program, to be known as the Tribal Continuum of Care Participation Grant Program, to provide competitive grants to eligible entities for participating in a continuum of care program under subtitle C of title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381 et seq.), either as a collaborative applicant or as a project applicant through a local continuum of care competition.

The purpose of the Program is to ensure dedicated funding is available to eligible entities working to address homelessness and housing instability affecting Indian tribes and Tribal communities through participation in the continuum of care program under subtitle C of title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381 et seq.), including as a collaborative applicant or as a project applicant within a continuum of care.

subparagraph.text: Of the amounts made available for competitive grants under subtitle C of title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381 et seq.) each fiscal year, $25,000,000 shall be available to carry out this section.

Amounts made available under subparagraph (A) shall only be available for a fiscal year in which the total amount appropriated for competitive grants under subtitle C of title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381 et seq.) exceeds the amount appropriated for such grants for fiscal year 2026.

The Secretary may not reserve amounts under subparagraph (A) if doing so would reduce the amount available for competitive grants under subtitle C of title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381 et seq.) below the amount appropriated for fiscal year 2026.

paragraph.text: An eligible entity may use not more than 10 percent of grant amounts received under the Program for administrative costs.

subsection.text: Notwithstanding section 106 of the Cranston-Gonzalez National Affordable Housing Act (42 U.S.C. 12706), with respect to applications for projects to be carried out on reservations or trust land using grants awarded under this section—

paragraph.text: the applications shall contain a certification that the applicant consulted with each recipient required to submit an Indian housing plan developed under section 102 of this Act; and

Indian tribes and tribally designated housing entities that are recipients of awards for projects on reservations or trust land from such funds shall certify that they have consulted with the recipients required to submit an Indian housing plan developed under section 102 of this Act.

subsection.text: A collaborative applicant for a Continuum of Care whose geographic area includes reservation or trust land is not required to meet the requirement described in section 402(f)(2) of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11360a(f)(2)) in order to be eligible for assistance under the Continuum of Care program under title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11360 et seq.).

In administering the amounts made available under this section, the Secretary may waive, or specify alternative requirements for, any provision of any statute or regulation that the Secretary administers in connection with the obligation by the Secretary or the use by the recipient of these amounts (except for requirements related to labor standards and the environment), if the Secretary finds that—

paragraph.text: good cause exists for the waiver or alternative requirement; and

such waiver or alternative requirement is necessary to modify any requirements preventing the participation of eligible entities in the Continuum of Care Program under subtitle C of title IV of the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 11381 et seq.) or would expedite or facilitate the use of funds.

The evaluation required under subsection (a) shall assess the extent to which the availability of on-site child care in affordable housing developments—

paragraph.text: improves housing stability for low-income families;
increases workforce participation and employment retention among residents;
supports early childhood development and school readiness;
reduces barriers to accessing child care, including cost, transportation, and availability; and
produces other measurable outcomes for families, including impacts on health, economic mobility, and family well-being.

subsection.text: In carrying out this section, the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development and the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall consult with Indian tribes (as defined in section 4 of the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 (25 U.S.C. 4103)), tribally designated housing entities (as defined in that section), the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands (as defined in section 801 of that Act (25 U.S.C. 4221)), public housing agencies, and other relevant stakeholders, as appropriate.

Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall submit to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate, the Committee on Indian Affairs of the Senate, and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives a report that—

paragraph.text: summarizes the findings of the evaluation conducted under subsection (a); and

includes recommendations for administrative, regulatory, and legislative actions to improve access to affordable, high-quality child care for families residing in housing assisted by the Department of Housing and Urban Development, including in Native communities.

section.header: Native American Advisory Committee on Early Childhood
section.text: The Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 9857 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Native American Advisory Committee on Early Childhood

paragraph.text: The Secretary, acting through the Assistant Secretary for Children and Families (referred to in this section as the Secretary), shall establish within the Office of Early Childhood Development an advisory committee to be known as the Native American Advisory Committee on Early Childhood.

The Committee shall facilitate, but not supplant, government-to-government consultation between the Secretary and Indian tribes on matters relating to early childhood development of American Indian and Alaska Native children.
The Committee shall be composed of 15 members, appointed in accordance with paragraphs (2) and (3), as follows:

subparagraph.text: 1 representative from each of the 12 service areas of the Indian Health Service.
1 representative from the National Indian Child Care Association.
1 representative from the National Indian Head Start Association.
1 representative from a national urban Indian organization.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall appoint the members of the Committee from nominations submitted by Indian tribes, tribal organizations, urban Indian organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations.
To the maximum extent practicable, the Secretary shall ensure that—

subparagraph.text: members of the Committee—

clause.text: represent diverse geographic regions, including Alaska and Hawai‘i;
have expertise in Tribally led early childhood education efforts; and
have expertise in areas such as early childhood development, Tribal child care, or public health; and

subparagraph.text: not fewer than 1 member represents Native youth.
Each member of the Committee shall be appointed for a term of 3 years.
Members of the Committee may be reappointed for not more than 2 consecutive terms.
Vacancies in the membership of the Committee shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment for the remainder of the term.

subsection.text: The Committee shall—

paragraph.text: identify emerging issues affecting the early childhood of American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian children;
propose solutions and provide recommendations, with respect to American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian children—

subparagraph.text: to improve programs for Tribes that support early childhood education and development;
to improve access to child care;
to enhance culturally appropriate care; and
to strengthen early childhood data collection and surveillance;

paragraph.text: provide guidance on Tribal consultation for early childhood initiatives;
identify interdepartmental barriers and propose solutions for coordination between the Administration for Children and Families and—

subparagraph.text: the Indian Health Service;
the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services;
the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration; and
the Department of the Interior; and

paragraph.text: advise on integration of traditional American Indian, Alaska Native, or Native Hawaiian practices in early childhood development programs.
The Committee shall meet in person not less frequently than twice each year.
The Assistant Secretary for Children and Families (or a designee) shall attend each meeting of the Committee.
Not less frequently than annually, the Committee shall submit to the Secretary and the relevant committees of Congress a report on—

subparagraph.text: the activities of the Committee;
early childhood education and child care challenges affecting Tribal communities; and
recommendations for legislative and administrative actions.

paragraph.text: Not later than 45 days after receiving a report under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall submit a written response to—

subparagraph.text: the Committee; and
the relevant committees of Congress.

paragraph.text: Members of the Committee shall serve without compensation.
Members of the Committee shall be reimbursed for travel, subsistence, and other necessary expenses incurred in the course of carrying out the duties of Committee.

subsection.text: At the request of the Committee, the Secretary shall appoint such administrative and staff support to the Committee to enable the Committee to carry out the duties of the Committee.
Chapter 10 of title 5, United States Code (commonly referred to as the Federal Advisory Committee Act), shall not apply to the Committee.
In this section:

paragraph.text: The term Committee means the Native American Advisory Committee on Early Childhood established under subsection (a)(1).
The term Native youth means an individual—

subparagraph.text: who is 24 years of age or less; and
who is an American Indian, an Alaska Native, or a Native Hawaiian.

paragraph.text: The term relevant committees of Congress means—

subparagraph.text: the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate;
the Committee on Indian Affairs of the Senate; and
the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives.

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The terms elementary school and secondary school have the meanings given the terms in section 8101 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 7801).

The term education-related occupation includes the occupations of childcare worker, preschool teacher, teaching assistant, elementary school teacher, secondary school teacher, elementary school or secondary school administrator, and any other educational occupation approved by the Secretary of Labor for purposes of a registered apprenticeship program.
The term eligible entity means—

The term registered apprenticeship means an apprenticeship registered under the Act of August 16, 1937 (commonly known as the National Apprenticeship Act; 50 Stat. 664, chapter 663; 29 U.S.C. 50 et seq.).
The term Secretary means the Secretary of Health and Human Services.
The term teacher apprenticeship program means an apprenticeship program through which individuals receive accreditation or certification in an education-related occupation.

subsection.text: The Secretary, acting through the Commissioner of the Administration for Native Americans, shall establish a pilot program to provide grants to eligible entities to carry out teacher apprenticeship programs to address the shortage of education professionals serving Native American early childhood programs and Native American elementary school and secondary school students, particularly in remote or rural communities.
An eligible entity receiving a grant under this section shall use grant funds to carry out 1 or more of the following:

paragraph.text: The planning and establishment of a teacher apprenticeship program, including the creation of a unique community-tailored curriculum for such an apprenticeship program.
The support and expansion of an existing teacher apprenticeship program.
The investigation of efficacy of a teacher apprenticeship program in teacher retention and satisfaction and student outcomes (including student well-being).
Providing wraparound services to students in the teacher apprenticeship program, which may include the following:

subparagraph.text: Tuition.
Textbooks and other class materials.
Technology, such as laptops and internet stipends.
Childcare support.
Salaries or stipends for program staff, such as a coordinator or student mentors.
Any other activity, item, or service included in the student's cost of attendance, as defined in section 472 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1087ll), for the program.
The Secretary shall select not fewer than 5 eligible entities to receive a grant as part of the pilot program under this section.

In selecting eligible entities to receive a grant under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to eligible entities serving rural or remote communities with demonstrated shortages of teachers or in other education-related occupations.

paragraph.text: Each eligible entity desiring to receive a grant under this section shall submit an application to the Secretary, at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary shall reasonably require, including the following:

subparagraph.text: A detailed description of the program for which the grant is requested, including—

clause.text: the relevant degree or certification program for program participants;
the workplaces in which program participants will serve as paid apprentices;
mentorship plans for program participants; and
additional resources for program participants.

subparagraph.text: A detailed budget for the program.

A detailed description of the challenges faced by the community to be served by the program with respect to teacher and other educator recruitment and retention, and how the program will address such challenges.
A detailed description of a plan to be carried out by the eligible entity to evaluate the program supported with grant funds under this section.

In the case of an eligible entity that determines that the objectives of the program would be accomplished more effectively through a partnership arrangement with an educational entity (such as a school or preschool) at which participants will be placed in teacher apprenticeships, an identification of such entity as a partner.

subsection.text: Section 645 of the Head Start Act (42 U.S.C. 9840) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (d), by striking (d) and all that following through (3) Notwithstanding and inserting (d)(1) Notwithstanding; and
by adding at the end the following:

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, a Native Hawaiian Head Start agency that operates both an Early Head Start program under section 645A and a Head Start program may, at its discretion, at any time during the grant period involved, reallocate funds between the Early Head Start program and the Head Start program in order to address fluctuations in client populations, including pregnant women and children from birth to compulsory school age. The reallocation of such funds between programs by a Native Hawaiian Head Start agency during a year shall not serve as the basis for the Secretary to reduce a base grant (as defined in section 640(a)(7)) for either program in succeeding years.
Section 645 of the Head Start Act is amended by adding at the end the following:

An Indian tribe that operates a Head Start program may, at its discretion, establish selection criteria, including criteria to prioritize children in families for which a child, a family member, or a member of the same household, is a member of an Indian tribe, to enroll children who would benefit from the Head Start program.

A Native Hawaiian Head Start agency may determine eligibility for Head Start services without regard to family income. Such agency shall establish selection criteria, consistent with community needs identified pursuant to this subchapter, to determine which children shall be enrolled and prioritized for services.
The Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024, is amended by striking section 238 of division D (42 U.S.C. 9840 note).

subsection.text: Notwithstanding any provision of the Head Start Act (42 U.S.C. 9831 et seq.), the Secretary of Health and Human Services, after engagement with Native Hawaiian Head Start agencies that operate Native Hawaiian Head Start programs, including Native Hawaiian Early Head Start programs, shall promulgate regulations under such Act that provide flexibilities for Native Hawaiian Head Start programs (including Native Hawaiian Early Head Start programs) that are analogous to the flexibilities provided for Indian Head Start programs (including Indian Early Head Start programs), as appropriate, including with respect to impasse procedures, service areas, eligibility requirements, reallocation of funds across Head Start and Early Head Start programs, selection criteria, facilities, data systems, Native American cultural preservation and language revitalization activities, designation renewal, and replacement of grant recipients.

section.header: Bureau of Indian Education Behavioral Health and Wellness Program
section.text: Part B of title XI of the Education Amendments of 1978 (25 U.S.C. 2000 et seq.) is amended by inserting after section 1139 (25 U.S.C. 2019) the following:

section.header: Behavioral Health and Wellness Program

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term eligible recipient means any student or staff or faculty member at a Bureau-funded school.
The term program means the Behavioral Health and Wellness Program established under subsection (b).
The term Secretary means the Secretary, acting through the Director of the Bureau of Indian Education.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall establish a program, to be known as the Behavioral Health and Wellness Program, to fill existing behavioral health gaps across Bureau-funded schools, including dormitories.

In carrying out the Program, the Secretary shall provide to eligible recipients, subject to the availability of funding, and at the discretion of the leadership of the applicable Bureau-funded school—

paragraph.text: virtual counseling services;
a hotline available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for immediate crisis support relating to behavioral health;
crisis response and support services; and
such other behavioral health services as determined appropriate by the Secretary.

subsection.text: For purposes of providing any service described in subsection (c), the Secretary may enter into a contract, memorandum of understanding, or interagency agreement, as applicable, with—

paragraph.text: a relevant Federal partner; or
an entity that has a demonstrated record of providing behavioral health services and working with tribes, Bureau-funded schools, and Indian students.

subsection.text: The Secretary may provide training and technical assistance to Bureau-funded schools that implement services described in subsection (c) or any other additional behavioral health services.
The program carried out under this section shall be a continuation of the Behavioral Health and Wellness Program carried out by the Bureau of Indian Education that terminated on January 31, 2026.
There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out the program $8,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2032.

section.header: Alaska Tribal School Program

subsection.text: Section 5212 of the Tribally Controlled Schools Act of 1988 (25 U.S.C. 2511) is amended—

paragraph.text: by redesignating paragraphs (1) through (9) as paragraphs (2) through (10), respectively; and
by inserting before paragraph (2) (as so redesignated) the following:
The term Alaska Tribal school means a full-time public school program operated in Alaska by—

subparagraph.text: an Indian Tribe (as defined in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304));
a Tribal organization (as defined in that section); or
a public or public charter school that—

clause.text: operates specifically to serve Alaska Native students; and
has a resolution of support from an Indian Tribe (as so defined).

paragraph.text: The Tribally Controlled Schools Act of 1988 is amended—

subparagraph.text: by redesignating sections 5209 through 5212 (25 U.S.C. 2508 through 2511) as sections 5210 through 5213, respectively; and
by inserting after section 5208 the following:

section.header: Alaska tribal school program

subsection.text: In this section, the terms Indian Tribe and Tribal organization have the meanings given those terms in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304).
The Secretary shall establish a program within the Department of the Interior to provide grants to—

paragraph.text: Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations that operate a public or public charter school in Alaska that has been certified as an Alaska Tribal school by the Secretary; and
a public or public charter school operated specifically to serve Alaska Native students that—

subparagraph.text: has a resolution of support from an Indian Tribe; and
has been certified as an Alaska Tribal school by the Secretary.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall determine the amounts of grants awarded under this section based on a per-student formula determined through a negotiated rulemaking with Alaska Tribal schools in existence on the date of enactment of the Native Children’s Commission Implementation Act of 2026.
The formula determined under paragraph (1) shall consider—

subparagraph.text: the hours served per day by the applicable Alaska Tribal school;
the grades served by the Alaska Tribal school;
the isolation of the Alaska Tribal school;
the cost of living of the area served by the Alaska Tribal school; and
additional costs associated with Native language programs, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.text: Except as otherwise provided in this section, a grant awarded under this section may be used for any of the following:

paragraph.text: Expenditures for education-related activities, including school operations, academics, extracurricular programs, residential offerings, guidance and counseling, and administrative purposes.
Support services for the applicable Alaska Tribal school, including transportation.
Not more than 1 grant may be awarded under this section with respect to any Indian Tribe, Tribal organization, or public charter school each fiscal year.

paragraph.header: No acquisition of real property or construction
paragraph.text: A grant awarded under this section may not be used—

subparagraph.text: to acquire real property; or
to construct a facility.

paragraph.header: Indian self-determination and education assistance act
paragraph.text: Indian Tribes may include funding provided under this section in contracts or compacts made with the Department of the Interior under the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5301 et seq.).
Section 5212 shall apply to Alaska Tribal schools receiving a grant under this section.

If the Secretary determines that an Alaska Tribal school is eligible for assistance under this section, the eligibility determination shall remain in effect until the determination is revoked by the Secretary.
Each recipient of a grant awarded under this section shall complete, and submit to the applicable Tribal council and the Secretary, an annual report, which shall include—

subparagraph.text: a description of the activities carried out using grant funds;
information on how those activities supported student academic achievement, student well-being, and other student outcomes identified by the applicable Indian Tribe or Tribal organization; and
any recommendations on how to improve the program under this section.

subsection.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $5,000,000 for each fiscal year.
